dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Kamila, do you have a fixed morning routine, or does it change every day?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: I always wake up at seven, but honestly, I rarely eat breakfast. I usually just grab a coffee and run.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Really? I never skip breakfast. I always have porridge with fruit. It takes about ten minutes, but it's worth it.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: I know I should. I sometimes feel dizzy by 10 a.m. because I haven't eaten anything.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: I'm somewhere in the middle. I usually have toast or an egg if I have time. But I always, always review my notes from the day before — even if it's just for five minutes.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: Oh, I do that too! I find that I remember things so much better when I review them in the morning.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: I rarely do that, I have to admit. I usually check my phone first — messages, social media. Bad habit.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: I never check my phone before I've had coffee and reviewed my notes. That's my rule. Social media can wait.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: What about exercise? Do you work out in the mornings?

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: I go for a run three times a week — usually Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. About twenty minutes. It wakes me up.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: I don't run in the mornings. I sometimes do push-ups in my room — maybe ten or fifteen minutes. Nothing serious.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: I go to the campus gym twice a week after classes. Morning exercise doesn't work for me — I'm not a morning person.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: How do you both stay focused during long lectures? I often find myself drifting off after about forty minutes.

dialogue.speaker: Amir
dialogue.text: I always sit in the front row. If the professor can see me, I stay focused. Works every time.

dialogue.speaker: Zhibek
dialogue.text: I take notes by hand. Writing things down keeps my brain active. If I type, I occasionally zone out completely.

dialogue.speaker: Kamila
dialogue.text: Good tips. Maybe I need to rethink my whole routine. Start with breakfast and go from there.

questions.text: "I ___ check my phone before I've had coffee." Which adverb fits Amir's rule?
questions.hint: "I never check my phone before I've had coffee." Never = 0% of the time.

questions.text: Where does an adverb of frequency go with the verb "to be"?
opts: At the end of the sentence
questions.hint: With "to be": subject + to be + adverb. "She is always late." NOT "She always is late."

questions.text: She ___ has porridge for breakfast. (= every morning, no exceptions)
questions.hint: always = 100% of the time. The strongest frequency adverb.
Adverbs of frequency go BEFORE the main verb (but after "to be"): I never check / She always eats.

questions.text: "I ___ do push-ups in the morning — maybe 3 times a month." Which fits?
questions.hint: "sometimes" = less than 50% of the time. Amir does this only occasionally.

questions.text: "She goes rarely to the gym." is a correct English sentence.
questions.hint: Incorrect word order! Correct: "She rarely goes to the gym." — adverb before main verb.

questions.text: He ___ arrives late — maybe once a semester. (= almost never)
questions.hint: rarely = very infrequently, almost never. Less than "sometimes".

questions.text: Order from most to least frequent: always / sometimes / rarely / usually
questions.hint: always (100%) → usually (80%) → often (60%) → sometimes (40%) → rarely (10%) → never (0%)
